title: LumenPath procurement onboarding - rate card & MSA clarifications
topics: Pricing rate card and committed discounts
summary: Procurement + security + legal from LumenPath reviewed Redwood commercial terms. Primary blockers: indemnity language in MSA, data residency clause in DPA, clarity on egress pricing for on-prem replication, and SLA credit calculation. Customer prefers VPC/private deployment but is open to hosted API for a pilot if DPA and KMS flow are acceptable. Next steps are to send redlined MSA, a detailed rate card showing committed vs on-demand pricing, and schedule a technical deep dive to validate connectivity and KMS integration.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Kim: Good morning everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros — i'm avery from Redwood AE, marcus is on the technical side.
[00:12] Olivia Carter: Hi, Olivia from procurement. We have Maya on legal and Diego on security, Samir from finance and nina on ML. Thanks.
[00:22] Marcus Nguyen: hey all. quick note - we'll keep the tech deep dive separate, today we're focusing on contractual and pricing clarity.
[00:34] Maya Liu: high level — LumenPath needs a clean path to sign. MSA has two sticking points: indemnity / third party claims and the data residency clause in the DPA. we also want specifics on SLA credits, how they're calculated.
[00:48] Avery Kim: understood. From Redwood side we can walk through the standard MSA redlines we accept. indemnity is negotiable to an extent — can you clarify specific language you need?
[01:03] Maya Liu: right now the clause is broad. we need limitation for indirect damages and a carve for customer data processed in a private deployment.
[01:14] Marcus Nguyen: technically that maps to whether you're using Redwood Private or hosted. for Private (VPC / on-prem) you keep control of keys; that helps with liabilities tied to data exposure.
[01:28] Diego Ramos: on keys — we require a KMS/HSM integration and explicit wording that customer-managed KMS is used for private. also, can you confirm no plaintext logs leave our VPC?
[01:42] Priya Shah: yes — for Private deployment we integrate with your KMS, logs are configurable and there is an option to disable telemetry. we can supply SOC2 artifacts and a security pack.
[01:53] Samir Khan: pricing — we need to compare hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved capacity. show us committed discounts, and also how egress will be billed if we replicate model outputs to our data lake.
[02:05] Avery Kim: absolutely. quick preview — our rate card has three bands: hosted on-demand, reserved Dedicated (monthly commit), and private (license + infra). egress fees depend on region and whether data transfer stays inside your VPC. i'll send a detailed sheet.
[02:21] Nina Patel: performance is non-negotiable for real-time features. what are the SLA numbers and how do credits apply? we need deterministic p50/p95 p99 latencies for the chosen config.
[02:36] Marcus Nguyen: our SLA for hosted is 99.9% availability for API endpoints, with credits scaled by outage minutes. for Dedicated we have tighter SLOs in the committed contract; we can include latency SLOs per model class in the SOW.
[02:50] Maya Liu: can you point to the exact SLA language? we need the remedy scheme in the MSA not a separate doc.
[02:58] Avery Kim: yep, we'll embed the table into the MSA exhibit.
[03:04] Olivia Carter: also, our procurement has a preferred term about data deletion on contract termination — how quickly can Redwood purge customer data from backups and caches?
[03:17] Priya Shah: standard is 30 days for hosted; for Private we can agree to an operational runbook to scrub KV caches and snapshots at termination.
[03:28] Diego Ramos: DPA-wise, we need data residency guarantees for EU-PAX and controls for audit logs — can Redwood support per-region tenancy?
[03:40] Marcus Nguyen: we support region pinning and can provide audit log streaming to your SIEM via an encrypted forwarder.
[03:47] Maya Liu: on indemnity again - we prefer mutual IP indemnity with caps tied to the contract value not revenue.
[03:58] Avery Kim: noted, i'll flag that in the redline we send.
[04:03] Samir Khan: about pricing: during pilot we'll only need hosted, but the P50 traffic shows bursty peaks. will Redwood allow a mixed approach — hosted for pilot and Dedicated after the commit?
[04:16] Avery Kim: yes, typical path is pilot on hosted with lock-in-free pilot credits, then transition to Dedicated with a notice period. we offer a 10-20% onboarding credit usually.
[04:29] Nina Patel: what's the baseline discount at annual commit?
[04:33] Avery Kim: depends on commit size. ballpark: 20% for 12-month modest commit, 30%+ for larger multi-year. we'll provide exact tiered bands.
[04:43] Maya Liu: legal will need to review escrow and source access clauses for conservation of service in the event Redwood undergoes acquisition.
[04:55] Priya Shah: we have an escrow program for critical customers; can detail that.
[05:00] Olivia Carter: egress — if we choose Private and replicate outputs to our S3 in eu-west, do you charge egress?
[05:10] Marcus Nguyen: if the traffic stays within your VPC there's no public egress; cross-region replication can incur cloud provider egress charges — we'll model that in the rate sheet.
[05:21] Diego Ramos: also need to ensure audit trail for admin RBAC changes, MFA enforced for Redwood console access.
[05:31] Priya Shah: we support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, MFA enforced via your IdP, and role-based access.
[05:41] Maya Liu: can you send the SOC2 cert and pen test summary?
[05:45] Priya Shah: yes, link in follow-up.
[05:48] Avery Kim: let's talk timing — procurement wants signed terms before end of Q4. is that realistic?
[05:56] Olivia Carter: yes if security and pricing are cleared by mid-October.
[06:00] Avery Kim: great, we'll target that.
[06:05] Marcus Nguyen: technical deep dive — propose week of Oct 12th to validate KMS flow and network path.
[06:11] Nina Patel: works for ML team.
[06:14] Maya Liu: one more — any limitation on model weights export? we need to ensure models can't be exfiltrated in raw form.
[06:24] Marcus Nguyen: model weights are hosted artifacts and can't be downloaded from hosted endpoints; for Private deployments you manage model artifacts. we'll document controls.
[06:35] Samir Khan: finance wants a simple total cost of ownership example comparing hosted vs Dedicated for 1M requests/month.
[06:45] Avery Kim: will include an example in the rate card.
[06:49] Olivia Carter: ok last question — do you support a trial NDA or mutual confidentiality before sharing SOC docs?
[06:57] Priya Shah: yes we can do a short mutual NDA.
[07:00] Maya Liu: good.
[07:03] Avery Kim: recap — we'll send (1) redlined MSA template with suggested indemnity and SLA exhibit, (2) detailed rate card with commit tiers and egress scenarios, (3) security pack + SOC2, pen test, (4) proposed dates for tech deep dive and pilot SOW.
[07:23] Olivia Carter: thanks, that covers it.
[07:28] Maya Liu: we'll review and get back with redlines.
[07:32] Avery Kim: thanks everyone.
